tier_reason: First-party real-site benchmark (ab against laruence.com, Yac drop-in vs Memcached drop-in) with the command and table published, but no CPU model, no compiler/flags and no runnable harness. Yac's own microbenchmark (bench/mp_bench.php, bench/run_mp.sh; Apple M5 Pro) has public code and a CPU model, but no compiler or flags and a >50x gain, so it also stays at C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: +18.6% to +20.1% RPS (141.6 vs 118.7 at c=20, 140.6 vs 118.5 at c=50, 142.1 vs 118.4 at c=100) and ~16-17% lower p50 latency (e.g. 699ms vs 840ms at c=100; derived from page data, the README summarizes it as ~15%); cross-checked with a fixed-count run (ab -n 10000 -c 100): 141.8 vs 120.6 RPS, +17.6%
corrections.hardware: 8-core / 31 GB server running PHP 8.1 FPM behind Nginx (per docs/blog-yac-object-cache.md); exact CPU model not stated
corrections.workload: Full WordPress homepage renders under `ab -t 30 -c <concurrency>` at 20/50/100 concurrent users on the author's live site (laruence.com), PHP 8.1 FPM, 8 cores. Each run starts from a flushed cache, a restarted php-fpm and a 500-request warmup, and only the object-cache drop-in differs (Yac vs the classic Memcached drop-in on localhost:11211).
corrections.caveats: This is a real-site benchmark from the plugin author's own README/blog and has not been independently reproduced. It gives no CPU model and no compiler flags, and it covers a single site. Throughput saturates at ~142 RPS because of PHP rendering and MySQL, so the ~19% gain reflects the localhost TCP round trips the drop-in removes. Separately, the yac core repo's bench/README.md (code in bench/mp_bench.php and bench/run_mp.sh; Apple M5 Pro 15-core, PHP 8.5, memcached 1.6.45 on 127.0.0.1) reports 169.6x-726.7x higher aggregate ops/s than local Memcached and 13.4x-69.8x higher than APCu 5.1.28, using 16 forked workers at a 100:1 read:write ratio. That figure does come with a stated methodology. It is not used as the headline because the compiler and flags are unstated and it pits in-process shared memory against per-worker TCP connections, so it mostly measures network round-trip cost. The wp-yac-cache plugin is GPL-2.0-or-later; yac core is PHP-3.01 (GitHub reports NOASSERTION).

notes: The original benchmark_url returns 404 because the repo's default branch is master, not main; corrected. All RPS numbers match the README table exactly. The record's '15-19% lower p50' was slightly off: it is 16.0-16.8% from the table. The caveat that the 170x-730x claim had 'no methodology' was wrong, because yac/bench/README.md documents it with code and hardware. The HN story 49680028 (2026-09-13, 2 points) links the plugin and quotes ~19%. Metadata checked: 833 stars, last commit 2026-09-24, not a fork, not archived.
